name: New Caledonian Javanese
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Roosman, Raden S. 1971. The Javanese immigrant community in New Caledonia: a preliminary survey. Te Reo 14: 63-73.
sources.note: p.66, section 'The speech of the New Caledonian Javanese': NC-born Javanese 'speak their Javanese with an unmistakable French accent and intonation'; 'the question of the nature of phonic interference will be taken up in some detail, when further research has been undertaken.' No statement of where word stress falls. p.65 gives the dialect background (Banyumas 'a-Javanese' plus other Central/East Javanese dialects; ngoko and 'village kromo' registers).

sources.citation: Subiyantoro, Marsono & Wening Udasmoro. 2017. Integration of French lexicons in New Caledonian Javanese. Humaniora 29(1): 85-93. doi:10.22146/jh.22568
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. pp.88-89 list only segmental adaptations of French loans (French /ø/>[ə], /y/>[u], nasal vowels > V+[ŋ], /f/>[p], /v/>[w], /ʒ/>[z], /ʁ/>[r], /ʃ/>[s]) and morphosyntactic integration.

sources.citation: Subiyantoro. 2014. Survival strategies of the Javanese language in New Caledonia. Humaniora 26(1): 43-55.
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic: ngoko-only oral use, code-switching/mixing with French, language shift; only a generic remark that spoken language uses 'tone, intonation' (citing Chaer 2010).

sources.note: Nothing on NC Javanese phonology; id.wikipedia cites only Glottolog, Ethnologue and Subiyantoro et al. 2017.

sources.citation: Hayuningsih, Arifah Arum Candra. 2023. The Javanese diaspora in New Caledonia: From indentured labourers to a fractured community. PhD thesis, Universiteit van Amsterdam.
